note: SimulacraBench-shaped cards: respondent x question cells scored by cps_skill (log-loss skill), datasets tx_s1/tx_s2/me_s1/nh_s2. Numbers are illustrative, in the shape of the loss analysis (gapTable recoverable-to-best per dataset, noise floor 2 SE).

cards.title: Per-dataset temperature scaling of the champion

citations.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks

cards.model: p_hat_T(y|x) = softmax(log p_hat(y|x) / T_d), T_d = argmin_T sum_{i in d} -log softmax(z_i / T)[y_i]

lossTerm.why: KL(p*||p_hat) contains a calibration part that a monotone per-dataset rescaling removes without touching ranking

assumptions: miscalibration is roughly a single temperature per dataset

estimation.method: 1-D Brent search on held-out log loss
estimation.crossFit: 5-fold respondent-grouped cross-fitting: fit T on 4 folds, score the 5th

expectedGain.derivation: nh_s2 headroom 0.012 x share 0.20 x recover 0.5 = 0.0012

algorithm.steps: collect champion logits per cell; per dataset fit T on training folds; apply on the held-out fold
algorithm.integrationPoint: post-processing after the stacker in predict()

prediction.statement: nh_s2 improves by at least 0.0005 paired, others unchanged within noise

cards.title: Respondent random-effect shrinkage toward the question prior
cards.model: logit p(y_ij) = f(x_ij) + b_i, b_i ~ N(0, tau^2); b_hat_i = (n_i / (n_i + sigma^2/tau^2)) * mean_j r_ij

lossTerm.why: respondents with few answers carry noisy residual offsets; partial pooling cuts their variance

assumptions: residuals are approximately additive on the logit scale

estimation.estimated: tau^2 by method of moments, b_i per respondent
estimation.crossFit: b_i estimated from the respondent's other questions only (leave-question-out)

expectedGain.derivation: tx_s1 headroom 0.004 x share 0.31 x recover 0.7 = 0.00087

algorithm.steps: compute out-of-question residuals; moment estimate tau^2; shrink; add offset to logits
algorithm.integrationPoint: logit offset before the final softmax

cards.title: Answer-entropy matching law for survey items
cards.model: p(y|x) ∝ p_hat(y|x)^a * q_k(y)^(1-a) with a = H(q_k) / (H(q_k) + D(x)), D the respondent's disagreement rate

lossTerm.why: the model under-uses the item marginal q_k when a respondent's history is uninformative

assumptions: item marginals q_k are stable across datasets
disagreement rate is measurable from training answers
cards.derivation: Minimise E[-log p] over geometric mixtures of p_hat and q_k; the first-order condition gives a as the share of predictive entropy explained by the item marginal, which reduces to H(q_k)/(H(q_k)+D(x)) under a Gaussian approximation of log-odds.

prediction.statement: the gain concentrates on items with high marginal entropy; tx_s1 improves and low-entropy items do not move

expectedGain.derivation: tx_s1 headroom 0.004 x share 0.31 x recover 0.65 = 0.0008

algorithm.steps: compute q_k and D(x) from training folds; blend in log space; renormalise

cards.title: Wider MLP head
cards.model: a wider network should do better

cards.title: Wild: score questions in reverse survey order
cards.hunch: respondents answer later questions in light of earlier ones; a reverse chain might expose consistency signals

prediction.statement: tx_s2 improves; if the chain carries no signal the paired CI covers zero

cards.title: Wild: answer like your nearest twin respondent
cards.hunch: copy the answer distribution of the most similar respondent in the training set
